content:
<mission>
Reverse engineer how Masefer's PUBLIC product catalog loads data (no login). Navigate the home page, open a couple of categories (/categoria/...), a brand page and a couple of product pages (/articulo/...). The site is a Meteor app: data likely comes over DDP WebSocket (/sockjs or /websocket) via publications such as categorias, metacategorias.web.all, articulos.parents, articulos.genericos, articles.web.one, subarticles.perParent, marcas. Goal: a TypeScript client that lists all categories and all articles with name, description, image URLs, brand, category and variants, without login.
</mission>

<start_url>
https://www.masefer.com.ar/
</start_url>

Start the mission by opening this URL.

## Workflow

Use this workflow as a guide — adapt as needed:

### Phase 1: BROWSE
Use browser MCP tools to accomplish the mission goal. Some available tools:
- `browser_navigate` - Navigate to a URL
- `browser_click` - Click an element
- `browser_close` - Close the browser
- `browser_evaluate` - Evaluate JavaScript code (also how to scroll)
- `browser_press_key` - Press a key
- `browser_run_code_unsafe` - Run Playwright code
- `browser_type` - Type text into input
- `browser_wait_for` - Wait for text/time
- `browser_snapshot` - Get accessibility tree (good alternative to screenshots)
- `browser_take_screenshot` - Take screenshot (prefer element-specific to avoid 1MB limit)
- `browser_network_requests` - List captured network requests

### Phase 2: MONITOR
Periodically call `browser_network_requests()` to monitor API traffic. You'll also get full traffic when closing the browser. Look for auth patterns (cookies, tokens, headers), endpoints, and response structures.

### Phase 3: CAPTURE
When done, call `browser_close()` to save the HAR file to: /Users/emimontanari/Work/Apps/sicor/spike/rae/har/e1d689cd924c/recording.har

### Phase 4: REVERSE ENGINEER
Analyze the HAR file at `/Users/emimontanari/Work/Apps/sicor/spike/rae/har/e1d689cd924c/recording.har` and generate the code. Extract all API calls, authentication patterns, and data structures.

Call `browser_network_requests()` frequently to monitor traffic.

content:
I built the client and ran it live against masefer.com.ar. It listed 4 metacategories, 48 categories, 30 brands and 551 articles. It also returned all 39 variants for the SNEAKPRO shoe. There is no free-text description to get, so `description` is always `null`.

Files are in `/Users/emimontanari/Work/Apps/sicor/spike/rae/scripts/e1d689cd924c/`:
- `api_client.ts`
- `README.md`
- `package.json`

**What the site uses:** the data comes over Meteor DDP on the raw WebSocket `wss://www.masefer.com.ar/websocket`. I didn't need the `/sockjs` path.

**Publications the client uses:**
- `categorias(["","",false])` and `metacategorias()` give the categories.
- `marcas(["","","",false])` gives the brands.
- `articulos.genericos([meta,"","",limit,"",false])` gives the articles. A limit of 100000 returns the whole catalog. Each article arrives once per price list (`PRECIOS_ID`), and the client merges these into one article.
- Images come in the same subscription, in the `dropbox` collection. They are keyed by the article code in `ownerId`, in two sizes (`/web/img200` and `/web/img500`).
- `subarticlesWithUniques([GENERICO])` gives the variants: color, size, SKU and stock.

**Auth:** none. No login, cookies or tokens are needed, so the script runs as is. It needs Node 22 or later, because it uses the built-in `WebSocket`.

**Caveats:**
- Documents keep streaming after the server's `ready` message, so the client waits until the stream goes quiet. A full listing therefore takes several seconds.
- `articles.web.one` returned nothing publicly, and the `articulos.parents`, `articulos.genericos` and `subarticles.perParent` publications you named were mostly unneeded. `subarticles.perParent` never appeared in the traffic.
- The API has no description field, so the article name is `DENOMINACION`.
- Fetching variants for every article opens one WebSocket per article. Use `listArticles("", true)` for that.
- I didn't run the HAR analysis step. I worked from live captures of the WebSocket traffic instead.
